They also announced that they would be working with [[Chris Goss]], who performed with [[Masters of Reality]] as an opening act the same evening.<ref name="newalbum">{{cite web|url=http://www.sacredsoul.us/cms/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=493&Itemid=95|title=Ian Astbury – The Cult new album...|date=23 January 2011|publisher=Sacred Soul|access-date=9 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005203639/http://www.sacredsoul.us/cms/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=493&Itemid=95|archive-date=5 October 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 11 May 2011, it was announced that the Cult were signed to [[Cooking Vinyl|Cooking Vinyl Records]], who would release the new studio album in early 2012.<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=157977 | title = The Cult Signs With Cooking Vinyl Records | work = [[Blabbermouth.net]] | date = 11 May 2011 | access-date = 11 May 2011 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110514165327/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=157977 | archive-date = 14 May 2011 | url-status = dead | df = dmy-all }}</ref> Commented guitarist Billy Duffy: "We are very much looking forward to returning to our U.K. roots in many ways working with Cooking Vinyl." Lead vocalist [[Ian Astbury]] added, "We look forward to a long and fruitful relationship with Cooking Vinyl." By May 2011, the band had been writing and recording new demos at its Witch Mountain studio hideaway in the Hollywood Hills, and began recording their new album at Hollywood Recording Studios.<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=158123 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20130104224249/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=158123 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 4 January 2013 | title = The Cult, Cooking Vinyl Records Comment On New Record Deal | work = [[Blabbermouth.net]] | date = 14 May 2011 | access-date = 14 May 2011 }}</ref> In October 2011, bassist [[Chris Wyse]] stated the album was almost finished and expected to be released in April 2012. Wyse also described it as a "[[Led Zeppelin|Zep]]/[[The Stooges|Stooges]] mix of energy."<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=164966 | title = The Cult's New Album Has A 'Zep/Stooges Mix Of Energy,' Says Bassist | work = [[Blabbermouth.net]] | date = 20 October 2011 | access-date = 23 October 2011 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20111124145956/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=164966 | archive-date = 24 November 2011 | df = dmy-all }}</ref>

On 29 November 2011, it was announced that the album would be produced by Bob Rock, who provided the same role on ''[[Sonic Temple]]'', ''[[The Cult (album)|The Cult]]'' and ''[[Beyond Good and Evil (album)|Beyond Good and Evil]]''.<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=166638 | title = The Cult Re-Teams With Producer Bob Rock and Mixer Mike Fraser For New Album | work = [[Blabbermouth.net]] | date = 29 November 2011 | access-date = 30 November 2011 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20111202213347/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=166638 | archive-date = 2 December 2011 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> The studio album, entitled ''[[Choice of Weapon]]'', was released on 22 May 2012. The band partnered with ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' to premiere the first song from the album titled "Lucifer" on 30 January.<ref>{{cite magazine | url = https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/the-cult-return-with-intense-new-album-20120130 | title = The Cult Return With Intense New Album | magazine = [[Rolling Stone]] | date = 30 January 2012 | access-date = 30 January 2012 | archive-date = 1 February 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120201051359/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/the-cult-return-with-intense-new-album-20120130 | url-status = live }}</ref> On 5 February 2012, the Cult song "She Sells Sanctuary" was used as the soundtrack for a [[Budweiser]] beer commercial in a mashup with [[Flo Rida]] aired during [[Super Bowl XLVI]]. In May 2012 the Cult appeared on ''[[Jimmy Kimmel Live!]]'' and played "For the Animals".

On 28 September 2012, it was announced that the band would release ''Weapon of Choice'', a "prequel" album to accompany the band's latest studio album, ''[[Choice of Weapon]]''.<ref name="Blabbermouth.net">{{cite news | url = http://www.blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=180067 | title = THE CULT To Release 'Weapon Of Choice' In October | work = [[Blabbermouth.net]] | date = 28 September 2012 | access-date = 28 September 2011 | archive-date = 7 October 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121007095234/http://blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=180067 | url-status = live }}</ref> The digital-only release, available exclusively on iTunes for two months only beginning 16 October, features the songs that were ultimately included in ''Choice of Weapon'' at an earlier stage of development. Explaining the motivations behind the release, lead vocalist Ian Astbury said that "These songs were turned over and over, forged in long rehearsals and writing sessions, and emanated from challenges both personal and professional. We put our guts into this; [Producer Chris] Goss was able to create an environment where the songs were born through playing and turning over lyrics, through hard work and intense sessions." Astbury added "These songs have an integrity and rawness of their own. In many ways it's a different album to the one we released and reveals the foundations of ''Choice of Weapon''. We were able to close the doors and begin to explore spaces we had not been in for a while."<ref name="Blabbermouth.net"/> The song "Twisted and Bleeding" was made available for free download at the band's website ahead of the full digital release.

On 20 June 2013, the band announced the release of ''Electric-Peace'' which comprises the entire ''Electric'' album plus the ''Peace'' album which was previously released on the now discontinued ''Rare Cult'' box set in 2000. It was released in the US on 30 July.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://archive.beggars.com/releases/220/the-cult-electric-peace | title = The Cult releases Electric-Peace | publisher = Beggars.com | date = 20 June 2013 | access-date = 20 July 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130619040216/http://archive.beggars.com/releases/220/the-cult-electric-peace | archive-date = 19 June 2013 | url-status = dead | df = dmy-all }}</ref> In 2013, Mike Dimkich left the band and joined [[Bad Religion]] to replace guitarist [[Greg Hetson]].<ref name="dyingscene">{{citation |title=Mike Dimkich leaves The Cult to continue filling in for Greg Hetson in Bad Religion|date=19 July 2013}}</ref> [[James Stevenson (musician)|James Stevenson]], from the ''Beauty's on the Streets'' tour in 1994, replaced Dimkich as the Cult's rhythm guitarist.<ref name="dyingscene" />

In March 2013, Billy Duffy told the Argentine journalist Fabrizio Pedrotti that the Cult had begun work on a new studio album for a 2014 release.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://fabriziopedrotti.com/2013/03/06/entrevistas-the-cult-nuevo-disco-en-2014/ | title = The Cult tendrá nuevo disco en 2014 | publisher = fabriziopedrotti.com | date = 4 March 2013 | access-date = 20 May 2013 | archive-date = 10 January 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180110175344/https://fabriziopedrotti.com/2013/03/06/entrevistas-the-cult-nuevo-disco-en-2014/ | url-status = live }}</ref> The band were expected to begin work on the album after they finish their 2013 world tour, where they played the ''[[Electric (The Cult album)|Electric]]'' album in its entirety.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://knac.com/article.asp?ArticleID=9482 | title = CULTS Announces Electric Album U.S. Tour UPDATED With Full First Leg Dates! | publisher = [[KNAC|KNAC.com]] | date = 13 May 2013 | access-date = 20 May 2013 | archive-date = 4 October 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131004223445/http://knac.com/article.asp?ArticleID=9482 | url-status = live }}</ref> In August 2014, Duffy added that the next album, which was not expected to be released before 2015 at the earliest, would "be more guitar heavy".<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cults-billy-duffy-thinks-next-album-will-be-more-guitar-heavy | title = CULTS' BILLY DUFFY Thinks Next Album 'Will Be More Guitar Heavy' | work = [[Blabbermouth|Blabbermouth.net]] | date = 24 August 2014 | access-date = 4 January 2015 | archive-date = 5 January 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150105003752/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cults-billy-duffy-thinks-next-album-will-be-more-guitar-heavy/ | url-status = live }}</ref>

On 5 November 2015, it was announced that the Cult would release their new studio album, entitled ''[[Hidden City (album)|Hidden City]]'', on 5 February 2016.<ref>{{cite news|title=The Cult To Release 'Hidden City' Album In February; Hear First Single 'Dark Energy'|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-to-release-hidden-city-album-in-february-hear-first-single-dark-energy/|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=6 November 2015|access-date=6 November 2015|archive-date=8 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151108172000/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-to-release-hidden-city-album-in-february-hear-first-single-dark-energy|url-status=live}}</ref> The album is said to be the final part of a trilogy<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/the-cult/89539|title=The Cult announce new album 'Hidden City' – hear single 'Dark Energy' now|website=NME.COM|date=6 November 2015|access-date=25 June 2016|archive-date=8 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151108214828/http://www.nme.com/news/the-cult/89539|url-status=live}}</ref> that began with ''[[Born into This]]'', and marks the fifth time Bob Rock had produced a Cult album. The band also announced that they had hired Australian-born bassist Grant Fitzpatrick (ex-[[Mink (band)|Mink]]) as the replacement for [[Chris Wyse]].<ref name="PBS Mink">{{cite web | url=http://www.pbsfm.org.au/Documents6c07.html | title=PBS Presents: Mink | publisher=[[PBS 106.7FM]] | date=November 2006 | via=[[National Library of Australia]] | archive-url=https://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20100510040249/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/15148/20100501-0018/www.pbsfm.org.au/Documents6c07.html | archive-date=10 May 2010 | access-date=8 January 2022 }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref name="blabber-Nov-5-2015">{{cite news|title=The Cult Completes Work On New Album, Introduces New Bassist|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-completes-work-on-new-album-introduces-new-bassist/|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=5 November 2015|access-date=5 November 2015|archive-date=7 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151107181608/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-completes-work-on-new-album-introduces-new-bassist|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Chris Chaney]] ([[Jane's Addiction]], [[Camp Freddy]]) and producer Bob Rock performed session bass on the album. In support of ''Hidden City'', the Cult opened for [[Guns N' Roses]] on the [[Not in This Lifetime... Tour]].<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Guns N' Roses Name The Cult, Billy Talent + More Openers for Summer 2016 Tour|url=http://loudwire.com/guns-n-roses-name-the-cult-billy-talent-more-openers-summer-2016-tour/|magazine=[[Loudwire|Loudwire.com]]|date=16 June 2016|access-date=4 September 2016|archive-date=23 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160623015730/http://loudwire.com/guns-n-roses-name-the-cult-billy-talent-more-openers-summer-2016-tour/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=The Cult to Open Both Dodger Stadium Shows|url=http://www.gunsnroses.com/news/title/the-cult-to-open-both-dodger-stadium-shows|publisher=gunsnroses.com|date=16 August 2016|access-date=4 September 2016|archive-date=17 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160917212831/http://www.gunsnroses.com/news/title/the-cult-to-open-both-dodger-stadium-shows|url-status=live}}</ref>

In an October 2016 interview with ''[[PopMatters]]'' journalist J.C. Maçek III, Cult guitarist Billy Duffy spoke of the band's playlist while on tour, saying "Obviously you want to make an impactful [show]," he continues. "There are some practical, pragmatic decisions made. If you're playing to a crowd who are not very familiar with you, there's no point of going too deep but we do always make sure we play a new song. Like on Guns N' Roses' [tour] we had fifty minutes which is ten songs all in. So, you know we just made sure that in those ten songs we played '[[Hidden City (album)|Deeply Ordered Chaos]]' which we're proud of and it makes a certain statement. And it just alerts people to the fact that, yes, we have made a record in the last 30 years. You know and that's a good thing. Psychologically, that's the blood transfusion that we need. And we're very mindful, we have a very loyal fan base. We don't pander as you well know."<ref name=PM>{{cite web|work=[[PopMatters]]|last=Maçek III |first= J.&nbsp;C.|url=https://www.popmatters.com/feature/hidden-city-to-hidden-cities-touring-with-the-cults-billy-duffy/|title=Hidden City to Hidden Cities: An Interview with the Cult's Billy Duffy|date=4 October 2016|access-date=21 April 2020|archive-date=30 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170830122406/http://www.popmatters.com/feature/hidden-city-to-hidden-cities-touring-with-the-cults-billy-duffy/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===''Under the Midnight Sun'' (2018–2022)===
In an April 2018 interview with ''[[Guitar World]]'', guitarist Billy Duffy was asked if an eleventh studio album by the Cult was in the works. He replied, "Never say never! Ian and I enjoy the process of making new music, and we feel it's vital to keep the band healthy, even if it's pretty much in the law of diminishing returns area now. Who knows if it will be a whole album a series of singles or an EP? I can say new Cult music will be forthcoming, but these days we don't rush it as there's no point. Quality is key. We are past the point of having to release stuff so if we feel it's good enough, then we will release it in some shape or another."<ref>{{cite magazine|title=The Cult's Billy Duffy on Gretsch Guitars, Tour with Stone Temple Pilots, Bush|url=https://www.guitarworld.com/artists/the-cult-billy-duffy-on-gretsch-guitars-tour-with-stone-temple-pilots-bush|magazine=[[Guitar World]]|date=23 April 2018|access-date=23 April 2018|archive-date=24 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180424010244/https://www.guitarworld.com/artists/the-cult-billy-duffy-on-gretsch-guitars-tour-with-stone-temple-pilots-bush|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 2 April 2018, a tour of the United States of America called "Revolution 3 Tour" was announced for the summer. They performed as one of the three headliners, along with [[Stone Temple Pilots]] and [[Bush (British band)|Bush]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/bush-stone-temple-pilots-the-cult-set-tri-headlining-revolution-3-tour-630040/|title=Bush, Stone Temple Pilots, the Cult Set Tri-Headlining 'Revolution 3' Tour|first1=Daniel|last1=Kreps|website=Rollingstone.com|date=2 April 2018|access-date=14 October 2019|archive-date=2 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210202214832/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/bush-stone-temple-pilots-the-cult-set-tri-headlining-revolution-3-tour-630040/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In April 2019, the Cult announced that they would celebrate the 30th anniversary of the release of their fourth studio album ''[[Sonic Temple]]'' with a world tour, which began on 2 May in [[Houston, Texas]] and was expected to wrap up in 2020.<ref>{{cite news|title=THE CULT To Celebrate 30th Anniversary Of 'Sonic Temple' With Special Los Angeles Concert In June|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-to-celebrate-30th-anniversary-of-sonic-temple-with-special-los-angeles-concert-in-june/|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=2 April 2019|access-date=24 May 2019|archive-date=5 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190405093656/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-to-celebrate-30th-anniversary-of-sonic-temple-with-special-los-angeles-concert-in-june|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=THE CULT Announces 'A Sonic Temple' Tour Dates In North America And U.K.|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-announces-a-sonic-temple-tour-dates-in-north-america-and-u-k/|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=9 April 2019|access-date=24 May 2019|archive-date=13 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413200037/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-announces-a-sonic-temple-tour-dates-in-north-america-and-u-k/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In a June 2019 interview with ''[[LA Weekly]]'', lead vocalist Ian Astbury stated that the Cult were "long overdue" to release new music. He was quoted as saying: "We do have some stuff we've been working on, but it's yet to see the light of day."<ref>{{cite news|title=THE CULT Is 'Long Overdue' To Release New Music|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-is-long-overdue-to-release-new-music/|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=13 June 2019|access-date=14 June 2019|archive-date=14 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190614024853/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-is-long-overdue-to-release-new-music/|url-status=live}}</ref> Six months later, Astbury told ''[[Atlantic City Weekly]]'' that the band was going to start working on new music in 2020: "We've got a few pieces lying around in various stages of completion. The intention is to get together in the New Year and take a look at what we've got and decide how we are going to go about moving forward. It's an essential part of any creative lifeblood."<ref>{{cite news|title=The Cult To Work On New Music Next Year|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-to-work-on-new-music-next-year/|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=11 December 2019|access-date=7 May 2020|archive-date=9 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809035024/https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-to-work-on-new-music-next-year/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 6 May 2020, the Cult announced on their [[Twitter]] page that they had signed to Black Hill Records.<ref>{{cite news|title=THE CULT Signs With BLACK HILL RECORDS|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-signs-with-black-hill-records/|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=6 May 2020|access-date=7 May 2020|archive-date=7 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200507133749/https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-signs-with-black-hill-records/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 15 August 2020, Duffy announced on his Twitter that the band were recording their eleventh studio album with producer [[Tom Dalgety]] at [[Rockfield Studios]], where the Cult had recorded their debut studio album ''[[Dreamtime (The Cult album)|Dreamtime]]'' 36 years earlier.<ref>{{cite news|title=THE CULT Is Recording New Album At Legendary ROCKFIELD STUDIOS|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-is-recording-new-album-at-legendary-rockfield-studios/|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=15 August 2020|access-date=16 August 2020|archive-date=31 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031054218/https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-is-recording-new-album-at-legendary-rockfield-studios/|url-status=live}}</ref> Progress was slow for nearly two years, hampered by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], and the album being recorded remotely, with the half of the band tracking it at Rockfield Studios and Astbury in the United States. In May 2022, Duffy told ''[[The Yorkshire Post]]'' that the "main bulk" of the album was finished and mastered.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/the-cults-next-album-will-be-quite-epic-and-big-sounding-says-billy-duffy|title=THE CULT's Next Album Will Be 'Quite Epic' And 'Big-Sounding', Says BILLY DUFFY|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=26 May 2022|access-date=28 May 2022}}</ref> On 7 July 2022 the band announced ''[[Under the Midnight Sun]]'' as the title of their album, released on 7 October, and "Give Me Mercy" was released its first single.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/the-cult-announces-under-the-midnight-sun-album-shares-give-me-mercy-single|title=THE CULT Announces 'Under The Midnight Sun' Album, Shares 'Give Me Mercy' Single|publisher=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=7 July 2022|date=7 July 2022}}</ref>

Prior to the release of the album, the Cult embarked on a co-headlining six-date UK tour with [[Alice Cooper]] and [[Creeper (band)|Creeper]] in May and June 2022,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/alice-cooper-and-the-cult-announce-co-headline-u-k-tour-for-may-june-2022/|title=ALICE COOPER And THE CULT Announce Co-Headline U.K. Tour For May/June 2022|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=14 September 2021|access-date=20 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/alice-cooper-and-the-cult-announce-huge-co-headlining-2022-uk-arena-tour-3045254|title=Alice Cooper and The Cult announce huge co-headlining 2022 UK arena tour|work=[[NME]]|date=14 September 2021|access-date=20 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://metalstorm.net/events/news_comments.php?news_id=43381|title=Alice Cooper - Announce Co-Headlining UK Tour With The Cult|work=[[Metal Storm (webzine)|Metal Storm]]|date=20 September 2021|access-date=20 September 2021}}</ref> and in the following month, they toured in North America with [[Black Rebel Motorcycle Club]] and [[Zola Jesus]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/general_music_news/the_cult_announce_us_tour_with_black_rebel_motorcycle_club__zola_jesus.html|title=The Cult Announce U.S. Tour With Black Rebel Motorcycle Club + Zola Jesus|work=[[Ultimate Guitar]]|date=11 May 2022|access-date=28 May 2022}}</ref>

===Reunion of Death Cult and potential twelfth studio album (2023–present)===
On 14 August 2023, Astbury and Duffy announced a twelve-date tour of the UK, along with a single US date in Los Angeles, under the title "Death Cult 8323". Whilst concentrating on the Death Cult material, the shows also covered [[Southern Death Cult]] and The Cult's first two albums, ''Dreamtime'' and ''[[Love (The Cult album)|Love]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Colothan |first1=Scott |title=The Cult revive Death Cult for November 2023 UK & Ireland tour |url=https://planetradio.co.uk/planet-rock/news/rock-news/the-cult-death-cult-uk-tour/ |website=Planet Rock |access-date=14 August 2023}}</ref>

On 5 October 2023, ''[[The Spokesman-Review]]'' reported that The Cult were working on new material for a possible 2024 release.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/oct/05/the-cults-ian-astbury-continues-to-grow-as-a-recor/|title=The Cult's Ian Astbury continues to grow as a recording artist|work=[[The Spokesman-Review|spokesman.com]]|date=5 October 2023|access-date=16 February 2024}}</ref> Astbury confirmed in February 2025 that new music from the band is in the works, but expressed uncertainty about releasing another studio album as The Cult: "Albums are dead, pretty much albums are finished. Albums are dead, the concept of making an album, I like the idea of making — if you have a piece of music and it's fresh, put it out."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/ian-astbury-says-the-cult-has-new-songs-in-the-works|title=IAN ASTBURY Says THE CULT Has New Songs In The Works|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=18 February 2025|access-date=18 February 2025}}</ref>

On 15 July 2025, the band announced a North American tour featuring a set performing music from Death Cult in addition to The Cult.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pearis |first=Bill |title=The Cult announce Death Cult fall US tour |url=https://www.brooklynvegan.com/the-cult-announce-death-cult-fall-us-tour/ |access-date=2025-07-16 |website=BrooklynVegan |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Artistry==
===Influences===
The Cult cite their influences as "everything from [[the Doors]] to [[Led Zeppelin]]."<ref name="drownedinsound">{{cite web|url=http://drownedinsound.com/in_depth/4149853|title=If anyone's an institution in the cult its billy|publisher=Drownedinsound|first=Dom|last=Gourlay|date=9 March 2016|access-date=19 March 2018|archive-date=15 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200615015947/http://drownedinsound.com/in_depth/4149853|url-status=live}}</ref> On the band's early influences, Astbury recalled, "We literally went from the front of our record collections to the back. And then along the way we were drawn in by the likes of [[Public Image Ltd]], [[Joy Division]] and [[Siouxsie and the Banshees]]. You might not hear it in the music but it's there."<ref name="drownedinsound" /> They also cite [[Bauhaus (band)|Bauhaus]] among many other post-punk influences.<ref>{{cite web |first=Timothy |last=Finn |title=The Cult's Ian Astbury on the Doors, Bowie & why 'classic rock' is an insult |url=https://www.kansascity.com/entertainment/ent-columns-blogs/back-to-rockville/article104423871.html |website=The Kansas City Star |date=27 September 2016 |quote=Q: "What or who else influenced the Cult?"  Astbury: "The Cult grew out of a lot of post-punk influences, Joy Division and Bauhaus." |access-date=2 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702180144/https://www.kansascity.com/entertainment/ent-columns-blogs/back-to-rockville/article104423871.html |archive-date=2 July 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> Duffy also praised [[Johnny Thunders]] and [[the Heartbreakers]] for a major performance he attended in 1977 and Siouxsie and the Banshees who "always had great guitar players with killer riffs."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://louderthanwar.com/part-2-of-billy-duffy-from-the-cults-top-10-albums-that-shaped-his-life/|title=Top 10 Gigs in Seventies Manchester that shaped my guitar style – by Billy Duffy from The Cult|publisher=Louderthanwar|first=Mick|last=Peek|date=2 March 2013|access-date=19 March 2018|archive-date=2 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210202214844/https://louderthanwar.com/part-2-of-billy-duffy-from-the-cults-top-10-albums-that-shaped-his-life/|url-status=live}}</ref> Duffy also hailed [[AC/DC]] for "the power of a good three chord riff", [[Pete Townshend]] of [[the Who]] "in terms of commitment to stage performing" and [[Brian May]] of [[Queen (band)|Queen]] for using "'echoplex' tape delays to orchestrate his own solo".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://louderthanwar.com/top-10-gigs-in-seventies-manchester-that-shaped-my-guitar-style-by-billy-duffy-from-the-cult/|title=Top 10 Gigs in Seventies Manchester that shaped my guitar style – by Billy Duffy from The Cult|publisher=Louderthanwar|first=Mick|last=Peek|date=2 March 2013|access-date=19 March 2018|archive-date=25 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191125163045/https://louderthanwar.com/top-10-gigs-in-seventies-manchester-that-shaped-my-guitar-style-by-billy-duffy-from-the-cult/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Musical style===
[[AllMusic]] writer [[Stephen Thomas Erlewine]] states that The Cult "formed as a [[gothic rock|goth]] band" and later became "a stadium-filling [[hard rock]] act led by the shamanistic Ian Astbury."<ref name="BIOAMG">{{cite web | last = Erlewine, Stephen Thomas | title = The Cult Biography | website = [[AllMusic]] | access-date = 12 August 2023 | url = https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-cult-mn0000139908/biography | author-link = Stephen Thomas Erlewine}}</ref> American vocal coach [[Ken Tamplin]] added "the band's early sound was heavily influenced by [[punk rock]] and [[post-punk]], with their debut album, ''Dreamtime,'' released in 1984," on his website.<ref name="KTVA">{{cite web |date=3 January 2024 |title=The Cult Unveieled: a Journey Through the's Iconic Sound |url=https://kentamplinvocalacademy.com/artists-bands/lead/the-cult/ |access-date=30 June 2024 |website=Ken Tamplin Vocal Academy}}</ref>  Astbury said, "our music is just melodies and guitars. We're like [[Big Country]] and [[U2]], only better!" in 1985.<ref>{{cite web |date=1 November 1985 |title=Cult Chat |url=https://archive.list.co.uk/the-list/1985-11-01/28/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210202214827/https://archive.list.co.uk/the-list/1985-11-01/28/ |archive-date=2 February 2021 |access-date=15 August 2020 |publisher=The List}}</ref>

{{Quote box
| quote = The songs were too long and just felt bloated and self-indulgent. We'd gone back into the studio too soon, as the label just wanted us to keep laying golden eggs. In reality, we should have kept rehearsing and gone through a pre-production process. We knew something was not right, but didn't quite know what it was.
| source = &mdash;Billy Duffy reflecting on the recording of ''Peace'' during a ''Sabotage Times'' interview.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hill |first=Mike |date=2021-04-06 |title='Electric' vs. 'Peace': The Cult's Near Brush With Obscurity |url=https://clrvynt.com/the-cult-electric-peace-compare-contrast/ |access-date=2025-06-13 |website=CLRVYNT}}</ref>
| width = 35%
}}

The Cult's music evolved over the years, blending hard rock, [[psychedelic music|psychedelia]] and guitar solos with gothic rock on their second album, ''Love'' (1985).<ref>{{cite web |last=Lawson |first=Dom |date=26 April 2018 |title=The story of Love, or how The Cult divided their fans and defined their career |url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/the-story-of-love-or-how-the-cult-divided-their-fans-and-defined-their-career |access-date=3 February 2023 |website=[[Louder Sound]]}}</ref> The band continued this style on their next recordings, but was dissatisfied with the results of the sessions. The tentatively entitled ''Peace'' was scrapped in favour of the [[Rick Rubin]]-produced ''Electric'' (1987), which was The Cult's first foray into an [[AC/DC]]-influenced hard rock and [[heavy metal music|heavy metal]] sound.<ref>{{cite web|last=Wall|first=Mick|author-link=Mick Wall|url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/the-making-of-the-cult-electric|title=How The Cult's Electric helped save rock|website=loudersound.com|date=7 April 2022|access-date=13 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Christopher|first=Michael|url=https://diffuser.fm/cult-electric/|title=30 Years Ago: The Cult Turn to Big Rock on 'Electric'|website=diffuser.fm|date=6 April 2017|access-date=13 June 2025}}</ref> While the band continued in this vein with their next album ''Sonic Temple'' (1989), the first of many Cult albums to be produced by [[Bob Rock]], they leaned more heavily on influences from various genres such as [[blues rock|blues]],<ref>{{cite web|author=Metal Mike|url=https://sleazeroxx.com/reviews/the-cult-sonic-temple/|title=The Cult: 'Sonic Temple'|website=sleazeroxx.com|date=10 April 2019|access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ondarock.it/rockedintorni/cult.htm|title=Cult - biografia, recensioni, streaming, discografia, foto|website=[[Ondarock]]|date=3 June 2025|language=it}}</ref> [[progressive rock|progressive]]<ref>{{cite web|last1=Fendley|first1=Scott|url=https://smedmusic.substack.com/p/the-cults-glorious-three|title=The Cult's Glorious Three|website=[[Substack|smedmusic.substack.com]]|date=10 April 2019|access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref> and [[arena rock]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Lester|first1=Paul|url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/every-album-by-the-cult-ranked-from-worst-to-best|title=Every album by The Cult ranked from worst to best|website=loudersound.com|date=27 February 2023|access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref> The band were seen as a middle ground between [[alternative rock]] and [[glam metal]] in the late 1980s, but Astbury rejected the latter label.<ref>{{cite web |last=Meredith |first=Kyle |date=December 22, 2022 |title=The Cult's Ian Astbury: "We were never a hair band" |url=https://www.lpm.org/music/2022-12-22/the-cults-ian-astbury-we-were-never-a-hair-band |access-date=March 3, 2025 |website=[[Louisville Public Media]]}}</ref>

The Cult incorporated tribal rhythms on their fifth album, ''Ceremony'' (1991), and experimented with [[grunge]] and [[noise rock]] on their self-titled sixth album (1994), with its use of distortion and feedback. The band's seventh, and first post-reunion, album ''Beyond Good and Evil'' (2001) marked a return to the hard rock direction of ''Electric'' and ''Sonic Temple''; both that album and its predecessor also saw The Cult reunite with ''Sonic Temple'' producer Bob Rock.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Penfold|first1=Scott|url=https://loadedradio.com/the-cult-ian-astbury-billy-duffy-death-cult-show/|title=THE CULT's IAN ASTBURY And BILLY DUFFY Bring Back DEATH CULT For Upcoming Live Performance|website=loadedradio.com|date=14 August 2023|access-date=13 June 2025}}</ref> Still, the band are mostly seen as alternative rock,<ref name="KTVA" /> heavy metal,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1989/07/02/arts/reocrdings-the-cult-dons-the-armor-of-heavy-metal.html|title=REOCRDINGS; The Cult Dons the Armor of Heavy Metal|work=The New York Times|date=July 2, 1989|access-date=June 28, 2024}}</ref> arena rock<ref>{{cite web |last=Everley |first=Dave |date=March 30, 2022 |title=The Story Behind The Song: Monster Magnet's Powertrip |url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/monster-magnet-the-story-behind-powertrip |access-date=February 26, 2025 |website=[[Metal Hammer]]}}</ref> and as part of the first wave of [[alternative metal]].<ref name="Vice">{{Cite web |last=Heller |first=Jason |date=August 26, 2016 |title=Loud Love: Soundgarden and the Heyday of Alternative Metal |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/soundgarden-alternative-metal/ |access-date=April 28, 2025 |website=[[Vice (magazine)|VICE]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The band's latest two albums, ''Hidden City'' (2016) and ''Under the Midnight Sun'' (2022), return to their gothic roots, while retaining a hard rock style.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zukowski |first=Zenae |date=2016-02-12 |title=The Cult – Hidden City (Album Review) |url=https://crypticrock.com/the-cult-hidden-city-album-review/ |access-date=2023-09-15 |website=Cryptic Rock |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dent-Robinson |first=Nick |title=Cult – Under the Midnight Sun |url=http://www.pennyblackmusic.co.uk/Home/DetailsMobile?id=27416 |access-date=2023-06-01 |website=www.pennyblackmusic.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>

'''Alice Cooper''', also known as '''the Alice Cooper Group''' or '''the Alice Cooper Band''', is an American [[rock music|rock]] band formed in [[Phoenix, Arizona]], in 1968. It originally consisted of lead singer Vincent Furnier (who adopted the stage name [[Alice Cooper]]), [[Glen Buxton]] (lead guitar), [[Michael Bruce (musician)|Michael Bruce]] (rhythm guitar, keyboards), [[Dennis Dunaway]] (bass guitar), and [[Neal Smith (drummer)|Neal Smith]] (drums). The band was notorious for their elaborate, theatrical [[shock rock]] stage shows.<ref>{{cite book|last=Waksman|first=Steve|title=This Ain't the Summer of Love: Conflict and Crossover in Heavy Metal and Punk|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=LqDJjAeYxssC|year=2009|publisher=University of California Press|isbn=978-0-520-94388-9|page=76}}</ref>

The Alice Cooper band was one of the few [[glam rock]] acts to achieve mainstream popularity in the United States, rising to fame in 1971 with the hit single "[[I'm Eighteen]]" from their third album, ''[[Love It to Death]]''. Success continued with the US top 10 and UK No. 1 single "[[School's Out (song)|School's Out]]" from the [[School's Out (album)|album of the same name]] (1972). The band peaked in popularity in 1973 with their sixth album ''[[Billion Dollar Babies]]'', which topped the charts in the US and UK and produced three UK top 10 singles. The supporting tour broke box-office records previously held by [[the Rolling Stones]]. 

The band split up in 1975. Furnier legally changed his name to Alice Cooper and began a successful solo career. In 2011, the original Alice Cooper band was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]].<ref name=HallofFame>{{cite web |url=http://www.soundspike.com/news/article/1239-rock_and_roll_hall_of_fame_news_rock_hall_makes_it_official_alice.html |title=Rock Hall makes it official: Alice Cooper, Neil Diamond among new class |publisher=SoundSpike |date=December 15, 2010 |access-date=December 17, 2010 |archive-date=December 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101218190653/http://www.soundspike.com/news/article/1239-rock_and_roll_hall_of_fame_news_rock_hall_makes_it_official_alice.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Between 1999 and 2021, there were occasional reunions of the band before reuniting permanently in 2025 for their first studio album in 52 years, ''[[The Revenge of Alice Cooper]]''.<ref name="Blabbermouth 2025">{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/alice-cooper-reunites-with-his-original-bandmates-for-their-first-album-in-51-years-the-revenge-of-alice-cooper|title=ALICE COOPER Reunites With His Original Bandmates For Their First Album in 51 Years, 'The Revenge Of Alice Cooper'|publisher=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=April 21, 2025|date=April 21, 2025}}</ref>

==History==

===Formative years: The Spiders===
{{Infobox musical artist
| name              = The Spiders
| image             = The Spiders (American rock band).jpg
| origin            = [[Phoenix, Arizona]], U.S.
| genre             = {{hlist|[[Garage rock]]|[[rock and roll]]|[[proto-punk]]}}
| years_active      = {{Start date|1964}}–{{end date|1968}}
| past_members      = * [[Alice Cooper|Vincent Furnier]]
* Dennis Dunaway
* Glen Buxton
* John Tatum
* John Speer
* Michael Bruce
* Mike Hughes
* Neal Smith
}}

In 1964, 16-year-old Furnier, then a student at [[Cortez High School]], was eager to participate in the local annual [[Letterman (sports)|Letterman's]] talent show, so he gathered four teammates from his high school's [[cross-country running|cross-country]] team to form a group for the show: [[Glen Buxton]], [[Dennis Dunaway]], John Tatum and John Speer.<ref>Cooper describes in detail in his first autobiography, ''Me, Alice'', how he was tasked with organizing an act for the show.</ref> They named themselves the Earwigs.<ref name=superduper>Harkima, Reginald, Scott McFayden and Sam Dunn, dir. Super Duper Alice Cooper. Banger Films, 2014. DVD.</ref> They dressed up in costumes and wigs to resemble [[the Beatles]], and performed several parodies of Beatles songs, with the lyrics modified to refer to the track team: in their rendition of "[[Please Please Me (song)|Please Please Me]]", for example, the line "Last night I said these words to my girl" was replaced with "Last night I ran four laps for my coach".<ref>{{cite news |title=Alice Cooper bandmates reflect on their historic past |url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/entertainment/music/2015/06/06/alice-cooper-band-interviews-history/28625657/ |newspaper=The Arizona Republic |first=Ed |last=Masley |date=June 6, 2015}}</ref> Of the group, only Buxton and Tatum knew how to play an instrument—the guitar—so Buxton and Tatum played guitars while the rest mimed on their instruments.<ref name="rock lifestyle">{{cite news |title=Rock lifestyle caught up with Cooper guitarist Glen Buxton |url=http://archive.azcentral.com/thingstodo/music/articles/20110308alice-cooper-glen-buxton.html |newspaper=The Arizona Republic |date=October 1999 |first=Larry |last=Rodgers}}</ref> The group got an overwhelming response from the audience and won the talent show. As a result of their positive experience, the group decided to try to turn into a real band. They acquired musical instruments from a local [[pawn shop]], and proceeded to learn how to play them, with Buxton doing most of the teaching, as well as much of the early songwriting.<ref name="rock lifestyle" /> They soon renamed themselves the Spiders, featuring Furnier on vocals, Buxton on lead guitar, Tatum on rhythm guitar, Dunaway on bass guitar, and Speer on drums.<ref name=superduper /> Musically, the group was inspired by artists such as the Beatles, [[the Rolling Stones]], [[the Who]], [[the Kinks]], [[the Doors]], and [[the Yardbirds]]. For the next year the band performed regularly around the Phoenix area with a huge black spider's web as their backdrop, the group's first stage prop.<ref name=superduper />

In 1965, the Spiders recorded their first single, "Why Don't You Love Me". The single's B-side track was the [[Marvin Gaye]] [[Tamla Records]] hit, "[[Hitch Hike (song)|Hitch Hike]]". The single was released by local record label, Mascot Records, owned by Jack Curtis, a concert promoter who also owned the Stage 7 teen club which later became the VIP Club where the Spiders were the house band. At the VIP Club the band supported bands including [[the Lovin' Spoonful]], [[the Yardbirds]], [[Them (band)|Them]], [[the Animals]], [[the Kinks]] and [[the Byrds]].<ref>Alice Cooper Golf Monster (2007) ISBN 978 1 84513 358 0 p36</ref>

In 1966, the Spiders graduated from high school and after [[North High School (Phoenix, Arizona)|North High School]] footballer [[Michael Owen Bruce|Michael Bruce]] replaced John Tatum on rhythm guitar, the band released their second single, "Don't Blow Your Mind", an original composition which became a local number one hit, backed by "No Price Tag". The single was recorded at Copper State Recording Studio and issued by local micro-imprint, Santa Cruz Records.<ref name=superduper />

By 1967, the band had begun to make regular road trips to Los Angeles to play shows. They soon renamed themselves Nazz and released the single "Wonder Who's Lovin' Her Now", backed with future Alice Cooper track "Lay Down and Die, Goodbye". Around this time, drummer John Speer was replaced by [[Neal Smith (drummer)|Neal Smith]]. By the end of the year, the band had relocated to Los Angeles.<ref name=superduper /><ref>Alice Cooper Golf Monster (2007) ISBN 978 1 84513 358 0 p59</ref> In Los Angeles, the band's lifestyle involved regular car trips into the desert. Activities included shooting rabbits with a 0.22 rifle. In 1967, Neal Smith moved into the range of Furnier's rifle as the latter was about to fire. Smith was hit in the ankle. He has the fragment in his ankle to this day.<ref>Alice Cooper Golf Monster (2007) {{ISBN|978 1 84513 358 0}} p39-41</ref> Around this time, the band and three others were driving in Los Angeles in a van. An incident on the road caused the driver to lose control of the van and it went off the road rolling over four times. The van was destroyed, but all band members and the three other passengers survived without serious injury.<ref>Alice Cooper Golf Monster (2007) {{ISBN|978 1 84513 358 0}} p55-56</ref>

===New band name: Alice Cooper===
In 1968, the band learned that [[Todd Rundgren]] also had a band called the [[Nazz]], and found themselves in need of another stage name. Furnier also believed that the group needed a [[gimmick]] to succeed, and that other bands were not exploiting the showmanship potential of the stage.<ref name=superduper /> The legend is that the name "Alice Cooper" came from a session with a [[Ouija|Ouija board]], largely chosen because it sounded innocuous and wholesome, in humorous contrast to the band's image and music. However, in an interview with [[Mark Radcliffe (radio broadcaster)|Mark Radcliffe]] on the [[Radcliffe and Maconie]] show on [[BBC Radio 2]] on November 30, 2009, Vince Furnier described the incident with the ouija board as an [[urban legend]]. He said "We literally got that whole story about the witch thing the way you guys got it. It was like just pure urban legend. I heard about the witch thing probably the same day you did, but it was a great story."<ref name="auto">"[[The Radcliffe and Maconie Show]]." Guest Alice Cooper. BBC Radio 2. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00p36ry Episode 30 November 2009].</ref> Eventually Furnier adopted this stage name as his own from 1969 onwards, being referred to as Alice Cooper on the cover of the band's debut album.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.discogs.com/master/52896-Alice-Cooper-Pretties-For-You|title=Alice Cooper - Pretties For You|website=Discogs|date=1969 |access-date=May 20, 2022|quote=The cover says: "ALICE COOPER: vocals and harmonica"}}</ref> He recalled:

{{quote|1=We were called the Nazz and we found out about Todd Rundgren's band who were called the Nazz. So I said let's not come up with a name that's dark, because they're expecting that. I said, "What if we sounded like we were somebody's aunt?" It was kind of like the all-American, sweet little old lady name. And I wasn't Alice Cooper. I was just the singer in the band Alice Cooper, like [[Manfred Mann]]. Pretty soon everybody called me Alice, they just assumed that the singer's name was Alice. So, at that point, I legally changed my name to Alice Cooper. It was a total outrage at the time. Now it's a household name.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.shreveporttimes.com/story/entertainment/music/2017/05/08/singers-name-alice/101328758/|title='…the singer's name was Alice'|website=Shreveport Times|date=2017-05-08|access-date=2022-05-20}}</ref>}}

The singer considers the name change one of his most important and successful career moves.<ref name="auto1">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.contactmusic.com/news.nsf/article/cooper%20name%20change%20was%20the%20best%20decision%20i%20ever%20made_1049224 |title=Alice Cooper's name change |magazine=Contactmusic.com |date=November 7, 2007 |access-date=August 13, 2011}}</ref>

The classic Alice Cooper group line-up consisted of Furnier, lead guitarist Glen Buxton, rhythm guitarist/keyboardist Michael Bruce, bassist Dennis Dunaway and drummer Neal Smith – all former members of the Spiders. This lineup stayed intact through 1974.<ref name=superduper /><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vGJ7XmA8rjIC&pg=PA188 |title=History of Rock and Roll |first=Tom |last=Larson |year=2004 |page=188 |publisher=Kendall Hunt |isbn=9780787299699 |via=[[Google Books]]|access-date=October 13, 2015}}</ref>

The band's first gig that used the name Alice Cooper was on March 16, 1968, at Earl Warren Fairgrounds in Santa Barbara. The posters still showed the band as the Nazz.<ref>Alice Cooper Golf Monster (2007) {{ISBN|978 1 84513 358 0}} p57</ref> After a 1968 gig at the Cheetah club in [[Venice, California]], where most of the club's patrons left after hearing the band play just ten minutes, they were approached by music manager [[Shep Gordon]], who saw the band's negative impact that night as a force that could be turned in a more productive direction.<ref name="Harkima">''Super Duper Alice Cooper.'' Dir. Reginald Harkima, Scott McFayden, and Sam Dunn. Banger Films in association with Eagle Rock Entertainment, the Movie Network, and Movie Central. 2014 – documentary</ref> Shep arranged an audition for the band with renowned musical artist and record producer [[Frank Zappa]], who was looking to sign bizarre music acts to his new record label, [[Straight Records]]. Zappa told them to come to his house "at 7 o'clock" for an audition. The band mistakenly assumed he meant 7 o'clock in the morning. Being woken up by a band willing to play that particular brand of music at seven in the morning impressed Zappa enough for him to sign them to a three-album deal.<ref name="Harkima"/> "Frank was the only one who stuck out his neck for us, for me," recalled Furnier himself. "He was the one who said, 'Here's a band that everybody in the business is laughing at – I like 'em.' ... He was the outcast in [[Los Angeles|L.A.]] and so were we."<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=[[Mojo (magazine)|Mojo]]|title=Alice Cooper|date=March 2002}}</ref> The first three Alice Cooper albums were released on Zappa's Straight label.

Another Zappa-signed act, the all-female [[The GTOs|GTOs]], were encouraged to dress up the Alice Cooper band members in women's clothing and heavy makeup, and played a major role in developing the band's early onstage look.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sickthingsuk.co.uk/people/p-christine.php |title=Miss Christine |work=SickthingsUK |date=November 5, 1972 |access-date=April 8, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120420085327/http://www.sickthingsuk.co.uk/people/p-christine.php |archive-date=April 20, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In June 1969, Alice Cooper released its first album, ''[[Pretties for You]]'', which barely cracked the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' Top 200 albums chart at No. 193. The band was the subject of media criticism after Furnier threw a live chicken into the audience during the 1969 [[Toronto]] Rock 'n' Roll Revival Festival. The audience ripped the chicken, whose name was Dutchess, to shreds.<ref name=star20140424>Howell, Peter. "Toronto 'chicken incident' sparked rage". ''Toronto Star'', April 24, 2014.</ref>

In March 1970, the band released the album ''[[Easy Action]]'', which did not chart. Also in 1970, the band had two songs ("Titanic Overture" and "Refrigerator Heaven") that appeared on a Warner Bros sampler album, ''Zapped'', featuring acts produced by Zappa.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.discogs.com/release/1827704-Various-Zapped |title=Various - Zapped @ discogs |website=discogs.com |date=February 1970 |access-date=February 4, 2022}}</ref>

===Finding success===
[[File:Alice Cooper Killer Tour 1972.jpg|thumb|276x276px|The band touring for ''[[Killer (Alice Cooper album)|Killer]]'', 1972]]
Slow sales of the band's first two albums, as well as Californians' indifference to their act, led the band to relocate again in 1970, this time to [[Pontiac, Michigan]] near Furnier's original home town of [[Detroit]]. Here, their bizarre stage act was much better received by [[Midwest]]ern crowds accustomed to the [[proto punk]] styles of local bands such as [[the Stooges]] and [[the MC5]]. "L.A. just didn't get it," Furnier stated. "They were all on the wrong drug for us. They were on acid and we were basically drinking beer. We fit much more in Detroit than we did anywhere else."<ref name="metrotimes">{{cite news |url=http://www.metrotimes.com/editorial/story.asp?id=5479 |date=October 8, 2003 |title=Alice doesn't live here anymore. But he can't forget the Motor City. |first=Serene |last=Dominic |work=[[Metro Times]] |access-date=July 15, 2008}}</ref>

Hooking up with young producer [[Bob Ezrin]], Alice Cooper released the single "[[I'm Eighteen]]" in November 1970, and it became a surprise Top 40 hit by early 1971. The single's success convinced Warner Bros that the band could be a viable commercial act, leading to much stronger investment in the third Alice Cooper album, ''[[Love It to Death]]''. The album was initially released on Straight Records, but was reissued on the Warner label following its buyout of the imprint from Zappa, giving Alice Cooper even greater exposure. Under Ezrin's direction, the band's sound moved from psychedelic rock to a tighter, guitar-driven [[hard rock]] sound, even as much of the lyrical content continued to explore "decadence, perversion and psychosis."<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Alice-Cooper-American-rock-band |title=Alice Cooper – American Rock Group|encyclopedia=Encyclopaedia Britannica|access-date=May 15, 2019}}</ref>

In 1971 the band was doing its first headliner tour. Backstage at a gig in Florida, a young woman came in with a boa constrictor coiled around her arm. This gave Furnier a fright, and after experiencing this kind of reaction, the idea of using a snake in the stage performance began.<ref>Alice Cooper Golf Monster (2007) ISBN 978 1 84513 358 0 p83</ref> With ''Love It to Death'' and its follow-up album ''[[Killer (Alice Cooper album)|Killer]]'' both charting well, the band was able to afford a more elaborate stage show, including sophisticated props and elements of gothic horror, and they became a highly popular concert attraction in the US and UK over the next few years.<ref name = allmusic>{{cite news |url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/alice-cooper-mn0000005953/biography|title=Artist Biography – Alice Cooper|first=Stephen Thomas|last=Earlwine |publisher=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=May 16, 2019}}</ref> Calls by members of British Parliament in 1972 to have the group banned from performing in the UK only solidified the band's legend,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.alicecooperechive.com/articles/feature/alis/011019 |title=Loads More Mr Nice Guy |work=Alice Cooper eChive |date=October 19, 2001 |access-date=April 8, 2012}}</ref> and the next year's ''[[Billion Dollar Babies]]'' tour broke box office records. Cindy Dunaway (Neal Smith's sister who married Dennis Dunaway) designed the band's costumes and occasionally performed in the stage show (she was the "dancing tooth" on the ''Billion Dollar Babies'' tour).<ref>Walker, Michael. [https://books.google.com/books?id=wr_WOMXnsvQC&pg=PA45 What You Want Is in the Limo: On the Road With Led Zeppelin, Alice Cooper, and the Who in 1973, the Year the Sixties Died and the Modern Rock Star Was Born]. Random House LLC, 2013.</ref><ref name=legends>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=60Jde3l7WNwC&pg=PA100 |title=Legends of Rock Guitar: The Essential Reference of Rock's Greatest Guitarists – Pete Prown, HP Newquist – Google Books |via=[[Google Books]]|date=March 16, 1948 |isbn=9780793540426 |access-date=August 9, 2014|last1=Prown |first1=Pete |last2=Newquist |first2=Harvey P. |publisher=Hal Leonard Corporation }}</ref> A 1973 gig in São Paulo, Brazil, was performed in front of 158,000 people. The Guinness Book of World Records gave the band the world record for playing in front of the biggest indoor audience ever.<ref>Alice Cooper Golf Monster (2007) ISBN 978 1 84513 358 0 p102-103</ref>

Following ''Killer'', Alice Cooper released three more top ten albums, the pinnacle being 1973's ''Billion Dollar Babies'' which rose all the way to No. 1 on the US and UK album charts. The band headlined highly successful tours from 1972 to 1974, before breaking up. The band made so much money in 1973 and 1974 that Furnier appeared on the cover of ''Forbes'' Magazine in 1973. The article listed him among the highest-earning American "music superstars": "Lounging in a $160-a-day Beverly Hills Hotel suite, Alice Cooper, who's a he,  ..."<ref>Alice Cooper Golf Monster (2007) ISBN 978 1 84513 358 0 p111</ref><ref>''Forbes'', April 15, 1973. THE ROCKERS ARE ROLLING IN IT AMERICA'S YOUNG ARE SHOWERING MORE THAN ADULATION ON THEIR FAVORITES. THERE ARE AT LEAST 50 ROCK SUPERSTARS WHOSE INCOMES MAKE HAROLD GENEEN'S LOOK LIKE SMALL CHANGE.</ref>

===Breakup of the original band===
The original Alice Cooper band played their final show on April 8, 1974, in [[Rio de Janeiro]], Brazil.<ref>{{cite web |title=Billion Dollar Babies Gigography |url=https://alicecooperechive.com/gigography/billion-dollar-babies |website=alicecooperechive.com |access-date=December 6, 2020 |language=en}}</ref> There are varying reasons former band members have given for the breakup. Smith said the members wanted to take a year off to slow down and possibly do solo projects, and just never reunited. Cooper said there was disagreement over how much money to sink back into stage shows, which had become costly. Bruce contends that Buxton's issues with substance abuse, which at one time led him to pull a switchblade on the band's tour manager, likely hastened the breakup.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archive.azcentral.com/thingstodo/music/articles/2011/03/08/20110308alice-cooper-glen-buxton.html |title=Rock lifestyle caught up with Cooper guitarist Glen Buxton |first=Larry |last=Rodgers |newspaper=The Arizona Republic |date=March 8, 2011 |access-date=April 20, 2018}}</ref>

The breakup was made public in 1975. <ref>{{cite web|url=http://ultimateclassicrock.com/alice-cooper-muscle-of-love/ |title=40 Years Ago: The Alice Cooper Band Release Their Final Album |publisher=Ultimateclassicrock.com |access-date=August 9, 2014}}</ref> Vincent Furnier continued using his stage name "Alice Cooper", carrying on with a new group of musicians. He also adopted the name legally.<ref name=legends /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ilikeyouroldstuff.com/news/alice-cooper-has-revealed-the-only-musician-who-calls-him-by-his-birth-name|title=Alice Cooper Has Revealed the Only Musician Who Calls Him By His Birth Name…|website=I Like Your Old Stuff|date=March 9, 2021 }}</ref>
Bruce, Dunaway and Smith would go on to form the short-lived band '''Billion Dollar Babies''', producing one album – ''Battle Axe'' – in 1977. 

===Reunions: 2010-present===
[[File:Alice Cooper - SSE Arena Wembley - Thursday 16th November 2017 AliceCooperSSE161117-101 (37651359815).jpg|thumb|right|250px|The four surviving original members of Alice Cooper at Wembley Arena in November 2017]]
While occasionally performing with one another and [[Glen Buxton]], they would not reunite with Alice until October 23, 1999, at the second Glen Buxton Memorial Weekend for a show at CoopersTown in Phoenix (Buxton having died in 1997). They reunited for another show, with [[Steve Hunter]] on guitar, on December 16, 2010, at the Dodge Theatre in Phoenix.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VxuPXFuhBSQ |title=Alice Cooper – Dennis Dunaway Interview |publisher=YouTube |date=October 30, 2011 |access-date=April 15, 2015}}</ref> This lineup would perform together again (televised) on March 14, 2011, at the induction of the original Alice Cooper group into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]], as well as on May 11, 2011, at London's [[Battersea Power Station]] at the [[Jägermeister]] Ice Cold 4D event (webcast). Bruce, Dunaway and Smith appeared on three tracks they co-wrote on Alice's 2011 album ''[[Welcome 2 My Nightmare]]''.

A documentary about the band entitled ''[[Super Duper Alice Cooper]]'' premiered at the [[Tribeca Film Festival]] on April 17, 2014, and was scheduled to be screened at the [[Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival]] a week later.<ref name=star20140424 />

On October 6, 2015, a surprise reunion show took place in Dallas at Dunaway's book signing session. He was joined by Bruce, Smith, Cooper and [[Ryan Roxie]], who replaced the late Glen Buxton.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/goodrecords/posts/10153696574654700 |title=Good Records – Original Alice Cooper Group Snakes! Book... |publisher=Facebook |date=October 6, 2015 |access-date=October 13, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://ultimateclassicrock.com/alice-cooper-band-reunion-photos/|title=Check Out Exclusive Photos + the Inside Story on Alice Cooper's Surprise Reunion|publisher=Ultimate Classic Rock|date=October 7, 2015|access-date=October 8, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/video-footage-of-alice-coopers-surprise-reunion/|title=Video Footage Of ALICE COOPER's Surprise Reunion|publisher=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=October 8, 2015|access-date=October 8, 2015}}</ref> The surviving members of the band were set to record and release an album.<ref>{{cite web|last1=DiVita|first1=Joe|title=Original Alice Cooper Band to Reunite for New Album|url=http://loudwire.com/original-alice-cooper-band-reunite-new-album/|website=Loudwire|access-date=January 10, 2017|date=May 11, 2016}}</ref> However, the only material to surface was two bonus tracks on Cooper's 27th studio album ''[[Paranormal (Alice Cooper album)|Paranormal]]''.

The four surviving original members reunited again for a five-song set on May 14, 2017, at a show in [[Nashville, Tennessee]].<ref>{{cite web|title=ALICE COOPER Reunites With Original Band Members For Nashville Performance (Video)|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/alice-cooper-reunites-with-original-band-members-for-nashville-performance-video/|website=Blabbermouth.net|access-date=May 15, 2017|date=May 14, 2017}}</ref> The four reunited yet again later that same year for a UK tour.<ref>{{cite web|title=ALICE COOPER REUNITES ORIGINAL BAND FOR 2017 UK TOUR |url=http://www.alicecooper.com/alice-cooper-reunites-original-band-2017-uk-tour/ |website=Alicecooper.com|access-date=June 14, 2017|date=September 29, 2018}}</ref>

In 2021, the surviving members of the band reunited for Cooper's ''[[Detroit Stories]]'' album. Producer Bob Ezrin as well as Cooper himself have said that a new album with the surviving members would be possible.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kielty |first1=Martin |title=Original Alice Cooper Group Still Angry with Late Glen Buxton |url=https://ultimateclassicrock.com/alice-cooper-i-hate-you/ |website=Ultimate Classic Rock |access-date=April 12, 2021 |date=April 10, 2021}}</ref>

On April 19, 2025, it was announced that Alice Cooper had reunited with Michael Bruce, Dennis Dunaway, and Neal Smith for the band's first studio album together in 52 years, ''[[The Revenge of Alice Cooper]]''. Released on July 25 via [[Edel SE & Co. KGaA|earMusic]], it was produced by Bob Ezrin, and also includes previously unreleased contributions by original guitarist Glen Buxton.<ref name="Blabbermouth 2025" /><ref>{{cite web | url=https://themusicuniverse.com/alice-cooper-reunites-original-band-for-the-revenge-of-alice-cooper/ | title=Alice Cooper reunites original band for 'The Revenge of Alice Cooper' |website=Themusicuniverse.com| date=April 19, 2025 }}</ref>

==Musical style==
Alice Cooper's music is typically seen as "sleazy" and "gritty but anthemic" [[hard rock]],<ref name = allmusic/><ref name = UCR>{{cite web|url=https://ultimateclassicrock.com/forgotten-first-albums/|title=Forgotten First Albums: Rock's 61 Most Overshadowed Debuts|date=July 16, 2023|access-date=December 29, 2024|publisher=[[Classic Rock (magazine)|Classic Rock]]}}</ref>{{sfnm|Hoffmann|2005|1p=478|Mojo|2007|2p=284|3a1=Phillips|3a2=Cogan|3y=2009|3loc="Alice Cooper"}} but also as [[glam rock]],<ref>P. Auslander, ''Performing Glam Rock: Gender and Theatricality in Popular Music'' (Ann Arbor, MI: University of Michigan Press, 2006), {{ISBN|0-472-06868-7}}, p. 34.</ref> [[shock rock]],<ref>{{cite book|first=Niall|last=Ferguson|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QOe8DwAAQBAJ&dq=alice+cooper+band+%22shock+rock%22&pg=PA299|title=The Shock of the Global: The 1970s in Perspective|page=299|date=October 15, 2011|access-date=November 16, 2024|publisher=[[Harvard University Press]]|isbn=978-0-674-06186-6 }}</ref> [[heavy metal music|heavy metal]],<ref name="Walser11,16,78">{{cite book|last=Walser|first=Robert|url=https://archive.org/details/runningwithdevil00wals|title=Running with The Devil|publisher=Wesleyan University Press|year=1999|isbn=0-8195-6260-2|pages=s. 11, 16, 78}}</ref><ref>
{{cite book |last=Christe |first=Ian |title=Sound of the Beast |publisher=Allison & Busby |isbn=0-7490-8351-4 |pages=2, 16, 18, 19, 39, 56–69, 93, 304, 333 |year=2004}}
</ref> [[glam punk]],<ref>{{cite book|url=https://studiadecultura.uken.krakow.pl/plugins/generic/pdfJsViewer/pdf.js/web/viewer.html?file=https%3A%2F%2Fstudiadecultura.uken.krakow.pl%2Farticle%2Fdownload%2F8872%2F8141%2F28327|title=Glam "Heroines". Gaps in Glam Historicisation from Black Self-Feminised Musicians... to the Herstory of Glam Rock|publisher=[[University of Rostock]]|first=Katharina|last=Alexi|page=9|access-date=November 16, 2024}}</ref> [[proto-punk]]<ref name="dictionary">{{cite book|last1=Abjorensen|first1=Norman|title=Historical Dictionary of Popular Music|date=2017|publisher=Rowman & Littlefield|isbn=9781538102152|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6ZyrDgAAQBAJ&q=%22alice+cooper%22+%22proto-punk%22&pg=PA14}}</ref><ref name="waksman">{{cite book|last1=Waksman|first1=Steve|title=This Ain't the Summer of Love: Conflict and Crossover in Heavy Metal and Punk|date=2009|publisher=University of California Press|url=https://archive.org/details/thisaintsummerof0000waks|url-access=registration|page=[https://archive.org/details/thisaintsummerof0000waks/page/75 75]|quote=alice cooper proto-punk.}}</ref> and [[rock 'n' roll]].<ref name = furious>{{cite web|url=https://www.furious.com/perfect/alicecooper.html|title=ALICE COOPER precursor to punk rock|first=Axel|last=Wheeler|publisher=[[Perfect Sound Forever (magazine)|Perfect Sound Forever]]|access-date=November 16, 2024}}</ref> Their first two albums, ''Pretties for You'' and ''Easy Action'', have a [[psychedelic rock]],<ref name = allmusic/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tucsonsentinel.com/arts/report/081624_alice_cooper/legendary-rocker-alice-cooper-steers-too-close-comfort-tour-tucsons-ava-amphitheater/|title=Legendary rocker Alice Cooper steers 'Too Close for Comfort' tour to Tucson's AVA Amphitheater|first=Xavier|last=Otero|access-date=November 16, 2024|publisher=[[Tucson Sentinel]]|date=August 16, 2024}}</ref> [[acid rock]],<ref>{{cite news|first= Chris |last= Parker |title= The theatric practicality of Alice Cooper |newspaper= [[Indy Week]] |date= 20 June 2012 |access-date= 11 February 2017 |url= http://www.indyweek.com/indyweek/the-theatric-practicality-of-alice-cooper/Content?oid=3089249}}</ref> and [[experimental rock]]<ref name="Cope">{{cite book |last1=Cope |first1=Julian |title=Copendium: An Expedition into the Rock 'n' Roll Underworld |date=2012 |publisher=Fsber & Faber |location=London |isbn=978-0-571 27034-7 |pages=91–92 |quote=As a rock‘n’roll group, Alice Cooper were always so much more than those first two horrible/brilliant LPs – and even they were genuine experimental rock of the Frankenstein kind. That is, they fell on their face at least seventy percent of the time, but struggled ever upward towards some Doorsian light at the end of the tunnel.}}</ref> sound, more fitting for their then-label, [[Frank Zappa]]'s [[Straight Records]], but on ''Love It to Death'', they transitioned to a "motor city [[garage rock]]" style, that continued on ''Killer'' and ''Muscle of Love''.<ref name = furious/> Alice Cooper are seen as precursors to [[punk rock]], but also influenced hard rock, glam rock, heavy metal, new wave, gothic rock and the bands [[Sex Pistols]], [[Nine Inch Nails]], [[Ramones]], [[New York Dolls]], [[Guns N' Roses]], [[Devo]], [[Cheap Trick]], [[Ozzy Osbourne]], [[The Cramps]], [[Kiss (band)|Kiss]], [[Plasmatics]], [[Misfits (band)|Misfits]], [[White Zombie (band)|White Zombie]] and [[Marilyn Manson (band)|Marilyn Manson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rockhall.com/inductees/alice-cooper/|title=Alice Cooper|publisher=[[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]]|access-date=November 20, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-aug-23-ca-2815-story.html|title=Under Influence of Alice Cooper, Ramones|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=August 23, 1999|access-date=December 29, 2024|last=Hilburn|first=Robert}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bmi.com/news/entry/eighteen-forever-in-conversation-with-rock-legend-alice-cooper|date=November 20, 2017|last=Smith|first=Alex|access-date=December 29, 2024|title=Eighteen Forever: In Conversation With Rock Legend Alice Cooper|publisher=[[Broadcast Music, Inc.]]}}</ref>

Alice Cooper took inspiration from 50s and 60s rock, such as [[Elvis Presley]], [[Chuck Berry]], [[The Beatles]], [[The Rolling Stones]], [[The Who]], [[The Yardbirds]], [[Love (band)|Love]], [[The Doors]], [[Jim Morrison]], [[Pink Floyd]] and [[The Beach Boys]], but also proto-punk, such as [[MC5]] and [[The Stooges]].<ref name = allmusic/> Many people over the years have brought up [[Arthur Brown (musician)|Arthur Brown]] and [[Screaming Lord Sutch]] as obvious influences, but this has never been confirmed by the band.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sickthingsuk.co.uk/10-trivia/t-influences.php|title=Influences|publisher=SickthingsUK|access-date=November 21, 2024}}</ref>

'''Whitesnake''' are<!-- Per WP:ENGVAR, bands are treated plural in the British English criteria. Therefore, "are" should NOT be changed to "is". --> an English [[Rock music|rock]] band formed in [[London]] in 1978. The group were originally put together as the backing band for singer [[David Coverdale]], who had recently left [[Deep Purple]]. Though the band quickly developed into their own entity, Coverdale is the only constant member throughout their history.

Following the ''[[Snakebite (album)|Snakebite]]'' EP in 1978, Whitesnake released the albums ''[[Trouble (Whitesnake album)|Trouble]]'' (1978) and ''[[Lovehunter]]'' (1979), which included the live staples "[[Ain't No Love in the Heart of the City]]" and "Walking in the Shadow of the Blues". Whitesnake soon began to make a name for themselves across the UK, Europe and Japan, with their subsequent albums ''[[Ready an' Willing]]'' (1980), ''[[Live... in the Heart of the City]]'' (1980), ''[[Come an' Get It]]'' (1981) and ''[[Saints & Sinners (Whitesnake album)|Saints & Sinners]]'' (1982) all reaching the top ten on the [[UK Albums Chart]]. By the mid-1980s, Coverdale had set his sights on North America, where Whitesnake remained largely unknown. With the backing of American label [[Geffen Records]], Whitesnake released ''[[Slide It In]]'' in 1984, featuring the singles "[[Love Ain't No Stranger]]" and "[[Slow an' Easy]]", which furthered the band's exposure through heavy airplay on [[MTV]]. In 1987, Whitesnake released their [[eponymous]] album, titled ''[[Whitesnake (album)|1987]]'' in the UK, their biggest success to date, selling over eight million copies in the [[United States]] and spawning the hit singles "[[Here I Go Again]]", "[[Is This Love (Whitesnake song)|Is This Love]]" and "[[Still of the Night (song)|Still of the Night]]". Whitesnake also adopted a more contemporary look, akin to the Los Angeles [[glam metal]] scene.

After releasing ''[[Slip of the Tongue]]'' in 1989, Coverdale decided to take a break from the music industry. Aside from a few short-lived reunions related to the release of ''[[Greatest Hits (Whitesnake album)|Greatest Hits]]'' (1994) and ''[[Restless Heart (Whitesnake album)|Restless Heart]]'' (1997), Whitesnake remained mostly inactive until 2003, when Coverdale put together a new line-up to celebrate the band's 25th anniversary. Since then Whitesnake have released four more studio albums ''[[Good to Be Bad]]'' (2008), ''[[Forevermore (Whitesnake album)|Forevermore]]'' (2011), ''[[The Purple Album (Whitesnake album)|The Purple Album]]'' (2015), ''[[Flesh & Blood (Whitesnake album)|Flesh & Blood]]'' (2019) and toured extensively around the world.

Whitesnake's early sound has been characterised by critics as [[blues rock]], but by the mid-1980s the band slowly began moving toward a more commercially accessible hard rock style. Topics such as love and sex are common in Whitesnake's lyrics, which make frequent use of sexual innuendos and double entendres. Whitesnake have been nominated for several awards during their career, including Best British Group at the [[1988 Brit Awards]]. They have also been featured on lists of the greatest hard rock bands of all time by several media outlets,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vh1.com/shows/the_greatest/episode.jhtml?episodeID=62184 |title=Ep. 036 &#124; 100 Greatest Artists of Hard Rock – Hour 1 &#124; The Greatest &#124; Episode Summary, Highlights, and Recaps |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605050813/http://www.vh1.com/shows/the_greatest/episode.jhtml?episodeID=62184#moreinfo |url-status=dead |publisher=VH1.com |access-date=24 April 2014 |archive-date=5 June 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2015/09/21/top-25-hard-rock-acts-of-all-time-where-does-your-favorite-rank/ |title= Top 25 Hard Rock acts of all time: Where does your favorite rank? |publisher=The Mercury News |first1=Tony |last1=Hicks |first2=Jim |last2=Harrington |date=21 September 2015 |access-date=24 April 2014}}</ref> while their songs and albums have appeared on many "best of" lists by outlets, such as [[VH1]] and ''[[Rolling Stone]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rockonthenet.com/archive/2006/vh180s.htm |title=VH1: 100 Greatest Songs of the 80's |website=Rock on the Net |access-date=1 March 2021}}</ref><ref name="50Greatest">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/50-greatest-hair-metal-albums-of-all-time-162362/tesla-the-great-radio-controversy-1989-165437/ |title= 50 Greatest Hair Metal Albums of All Time |last1=Beaujour |first1=Tom |last2= Bienstock |first2=Richard |last3= Eddy |first3=Chuck |last4=Fischer |first4=Reed |last5=Grow |first5=Kory |last6=Johnston |first6=Maura |author6-link=Maura Johnston |last7=Weingarten |first7=Christopher R. |magazine=Rolling Stone |date=31 August 2019 |access-date=11 February 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |date=20 June 2012 |title=Readers' Poll: The Best Hair Metal Songs of All Time |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/readers-poll-the-best-hair-metal-songs-of-all-time-12979/9-whitesnake-here-i-go-again-256356/ |magazine=Rolling Stone |access-date=1 March 2021}}</ref>

== History ==
=== Formation, ''Snakebite'' and ''Trouble'' (1976–1978) ===
In March 1976, singer [[David Coverdale]] left the English hard rock group [[Deep Purple]]. He had joined the band three years prior and recorded three successful albums with them. After leaving Deep Purple, Coverdale released his solo album ''[[White Snake (album)|White Snake]]'' in February 1977.{{refn|group=nb|''[[White Snake (album)|White Snake]]'' was initially released by [[Polydor Records]] on 22 February 1977, followed by a re-release in May through [[Purple Records]].<ref>{{Cite web| url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/david-coverdale-solo-albums-white-snake-northwinds | title= "I have to prove that I'm capable of doing it, and I wasn't just being done a favour by Deep Purple": the two forgotten David Coverdale solo albums that sowed the seeds for Whitesnake |first=Neil |last=Jeffries |website=Louder | date=5 May 2024 | access-date=27 October 2024 }}</ref>{{sfn|Popoff|2015|p=17}}}} His second solo album ''[[Northwinds]]'' was released in March 1978.{{sfn|Popoff|2015|p=22}} Both combined elements of blues, soul and funk, as Coverdale had wanted to distance himself from the hard rock sound synonymous with Deep Purple.{{sfn|Popoff|2015|pp=14, 16, 19}} Both records featured former [[Snafu (band)|Snafu]] guitarist [[Micky Moody]], whom Coverdale had known since the late 1960s.{{sfn|Popoff|2015|p=15}} Moody was the first to join Coverdale's backing band, which he began assembling in London.{{sfn|Popoff|2015|pp=23{{ndash}}24}}<ref name="Early1">{{Cite web| url=https://whitesnake.com/early-years-part-1/ | title= Early Years Part 1 | website=Whitesnake Official Site | date=4 January 2016 | access-date=11 February 2021 }}</ref> As stated by Coverdale, "Whitesnake were actually formed to promote ''Northwinds'' on a one-off promotional tour".<ref name="Vain"/> Moody suggested bringing in a second guitarist, with the spot ultimately going to [[Bernie Marsden]], formerly of [[UFO]] and [[Paice Ashton Lord]].<ref name="Early1"/>{{sfn|Popoff|2015|p=24}} With his help, the band were able to recruit bassist [[Neil Murray (British musician)|Neil Murray]], who had played with Marsden in [[Cozy Powell]]'s Hammer.{{sfn|Popoff|2015|p=26}} The group's initial line-up was rounded out by drummer [[Dave Dowle|Dave "Duck" Dowle]] and keyboardist Brian Johnson, who had played together in [[Streetwalkers]].{{sfn|Popoff|2015|p=27}} Other early candidates for the band were drummers Cozy Powell and [[Dave Holland (drummer)|Dave Holland]], as well as guitarist [[Mel Galley]].{{sfn|Popoff|2015|pp=27{{ndash}}28}}

[[File:Whitesnake First Tour Poster.jpg|thumb|left|upright|A newspaper advert for Whitesnake's first UK tour, promoting [[David Coverdale]]'s second solo album ''[[Northwinds]]'' (1978)]]
The band, dubbed David Coverdale's Whitesnake, played their first show at [[University of Lincoln|Lincoln Technical College]] on 3 March 1978.<ref>{{Cite web| url=https://whitesnake.com/first-show-march-3-1978/ | title=40 Years Ago Today – Whitesnake's First Show |website=Whitesnake Official Site | date=3 March 2018 | access-date=21 February 2021 }}</ref><ref name="UCR">{{Cite web| url=https://ultimateclassicrock.com/whitesnake-first-concert/ | title=When Whitesnake Played Their First Concert |website=Ultimate Classic Rock | date=3 March 2016 | access-date=21 February 2021 }}</ref> Their live debut had originally been scheduled for 23 February at the Sky Bird Club in Nottingham, but the show was cancelled.<ref name="UCR"/>{{sfn|Popoff|2015|p=29}} Coverdale had originally wanted the group to be simply called Whitesnake, but was forced to use his own name as it still carried some clout as the former lead singer of Deep Purple.{{sfn|Popoff|2015|p=14}}<ref name="Trouble">{{Cite AV media notes |title=Trouble |title-link=Trouble (Whitesnake album) |others=Whitesnake |date=2006 |first=Geoff |last=Barton |author-link=Geoff Barton |pages=2{{ndash}}11 |type=booklet |publisher=EMI |id=0946 3 59688 2 8}}</ref><ref name="Mars">{{cite magazine |last=Oliver |first=Derek |date=March 2011 |title=Life on Mars |magazine=[[Classic Rock (magazine)|Classic Rock]] presents: Whitesnake – Forevermore (The Official Album Magazine) |pages=72{{ndash}}77 |publisher=Future plc |location=London, England}}</ref> In a 2009 interview with [[Metro (British newspaper)|''Metro'']], Coverdale jokingly stated that the name "Whitesnake" was a euphemism for his penis. In fact, it came from the song of the same name found on his first solo album.<ref>{{Cite web| url=https://bravewords.com/news/whitesnake-mainman-talks-about-origin-of-name-slide-it-in-tales-and-other-rock-n-roll-moments | title=Whitesnake Mainman Talks About Origin Of Name, Slide It In Tales And Other Rock N' Roll Moments |website=Brave Words | date=9 June 2009 | access-date=30 July 2021 }}</ref>

After completing a small UK club tour, the band adjourned to a rehearsal place in London's West End to begin writing new songs.<ref name="Early1"/> They soon caught the attention of [[EMI International]]'s Robbie Dennis, who wanted to sign the group. According to Bernie Marsden, however, his higher-ups were not ready to commit to a full album. Thus, the band entered London's Central Recorders Studio in April 1978 to record an EP.{{sfn|Popoff|2015|pp=29{{ndash}}30}} By this point, original keyboardist Brian Johnston had been replaced by Pete Solley.<ref name="Trouble"/> [[Martin Birch]], who had worked with Coverdale during his time in Deep Purple, was chosen to produce.{{sfn|Popoff|2015|p=29}}

{{Listen
|filename = Ain't No Love in the Heart of the City.ogg
|title = "Ain't No Love in the Heart of the City" (1978)
|description = Since its release, "[[Ain't No Love in the Heart of the City]]" has become a live staple at Whitsnake concerts with Coverdale referring to it as "the national anthem of the Whitesnake choir".<ref name="Ain't No Love"/>
|pos=right
}}
The resulting record, ''[[Snakebite (album)|Snakebite]]'', was released in June 1978.<ref name="Trouble"/> In Europe, the EP was combined with four tracks from Coverdale's ''Northwinds'' to make up a full-length album.<ref name="Trouble"/> ''Snakebite'' contained a slowed down cover of [[Bobby Bland]]'s "[[Ain't No Love in the Heart of the City]]", which had originally been used by the band to audition bass players.
